evidence: OpenStreetMap way 614516704 is tagged leisure=stadium, name=Ross-Ade Stadium, operator=Purdue University, and links to Purdue Athletics; geometry projects to a 217.07 m by 295.52 m outer stadium/site envelope.
The model reopens with a north-south field and a bowl/site outline whose 225 m by 305 m evaluated extents are about 3.65% and 3.21% larger than the OSM outer way bounds.
The supplied target_buildings_gis.json contains only LWSN, KRAN, KNOY, HIKS, and RAWL; it is not a Ross-Ade footprint source.
findings: Identity is clear, but the OSM leisure=stadium polygon is a broad stadium/site envelope rather than surveyed structural wall lines; the modest overrun cannot be separated from plaza or decorative geometry without a structural footprint overlay.

evidence: Manifest origin is (-403.2000, 805.2000) m. OSM way 614516704 projects to bounding-box center (-403.1939, 805.2177) m using the project Bell Tower origin and documented local conversion; center offset is approximately -0.006 m X and -0.018 m Y.
Read-only master inspection found Placement_ross_ade at (-403.2000, 805.2000, 0) m, zero rotation, unit scale, instancing Asset_ross_ade.
Evaluated geometry is 225 m east-west by 305 m north-south, approximately 3–4% larger than the projected OSM outer envelope; field is modeled north-south.
findings: Location/orientation are strongly verified; dimensions are close against an outer site polygon, with the reference limitation recorded under footprint.

criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
evidence: Reopened evaluated asset spans Z=-0.02 to 49.75 m; the press-box pavilion roof is around 36 m and floodlight heads reach 49.75 m.
Purdue Athletics confirms permanent lighting was installed in 2017 and describes stadium expansions/press box history; Purdue’s public page does not provide surveyed height or floor elevations.
Review render shows an open bowl, west pavilion/press box, south end zone, and four corner floodlight towers.
findings: Overall stadium form is plausible, but exact height, story levels, section profile, and roof elevations are estimates; no authoritative elevation/section drawing was located.

evidence: Purdue Athletics documents the 2018 field-level brick facade, permanent lighting, the 2023 south end-zone addition/Tiller Tunnel, and a 2020 south-end video board measuring 150 ft 4 in by 56 ft 9 in.

Reopened model includes brick-faced west pavilion/press box, gate structures, Tiller Tunnel, south end zone, lights, and a 45.82 m by 17.30 m south video screen, matching Purdue’s published board dimensions.
Three-quarter and top review renders are saved in audit/ross_ade.
findings: Major signature elements are present and the video board dimensions match the official source. Fine gate/facade placement lacks a source overlay; review renders show broad seating-bowl surfaces washed out to white, obscuring the seat pattern and reducing visual fidelity.

criteria.criterion: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
evidence: Saved file reopened successfully in Blender 5.2.3 LTS; scene Building_ross_ade contains collection Asset_ross_ade with 2,118 objects (2,117 meshes) and the manifest’s expected root/name.
Manifest records local coordinates and stable path buildings/ross_ade.blend; evaluated bounds agree with its local/world bounds. The root is at local origin.

No non-generated external image paths were found; the asset is self-contained. The audit records provider, feature ID, retrieval/source timestamp, CRS, conversion, measurement method, uncertainty, source URLs, and findings.
findings: Passes library naming, reopen, and portability checks.

sources.title: OpenStreetMap Ross-Ade Stadium way 614516704
sources.method: Project node lon/lat to local meters using origin (-86.9137, 40.4274): X=(lon+86.9137)*111412.84*cos(40.4274°), Y=(lat-40.4274)*111040. Compare axis-aligned outer feature bounds and center with evaluated asset bounds and manifest placement.
sources.uncertainty: Outer leisure=stadium polygon is not a surveyed wall footprint; local conversion is an approximation; OSM mapping date and positional accuracy are not survey-certified.

findings: The strongest evidence is identity, placement, north-south orientation, major signature elements, and a screen size matching Purdue’s published dimensions.
The OSM comparison is an outer stadium/site polygon, not the wall footprint; model XY extents exceed its projected bounds by approximately 3–4%.
Exact height, story elevations, and detailed facade/seat fidelity remain uncertain; the review render’s washed-out white bowl surfaces obscure seat detail.
